topIssues.title: go: default to RPC 127.0.0.1
topIssues.author: protolambda
topIssues.body:
Services all default to binding the RPC to 0.0.0.0 currently.
It's considered better to default to 127.0.0.1 to not accidentally expose an RPC publicly, like many L1 clients do.
This may break existing configurations, so this change should be coupled to a release, and goes into many releases (op-batcher/op-propoiser/op-challenger/op-node/op-conductor to name a few).

topIssues.title: [PCD] Predict L1 addresses via dry-run
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body:
The L2 genesis embeds the L1 proxy addresses for `L1CrossDomainMessenger`, `L1StandardBridge`, `L1ERC721Bridge`, `OptimismPortal`, and `SystemConfig`. Since these contracts don't exist yet when the genesis is built, their addresses must be predicted. OPCM uses `CREATE2` for every proxy, so the addresses are deterministic given the salt inputs. Add a pipeline stage that calls OPCM's `deploy()` as a non-broadcasting `eth_call` and reads the returned `ChainContracts` struct, then persists the addresses to state.   
Note: OPCM mixes `msg.sender` into the CREATE2 salt for every proxy, so the dry-run must be sent from the same key that will eventually broadcast the real deploy transaction. A dry-run from a different `from` produces different predicted addresses, and the L2 genesis built from them would be invalid.

topIssues.title: default syncmode.offset-el-safe to 12h fails for --minimal nodes
topIssues.author: Creamers158
topIssues.body:
Running op-node v1.19.0 + op-reth v2.3.1 on multiple Superchain registry chains (Zora, BOB, Mode, etc.) with `--syncmode=execution-layer` Repeatedly seeing:

```
lvl=warn msg="Failed to insert unsafe payload for EL sync"
err="temp: EL sync offset-derived head at block XXXXXXX: l2 block is missing L1 info deposit tx, block hash: 0x..."
```
The error advances block-by-block and never resolves. Switching to `--syncmode=consensus-layer` masks it.

Setting `--syncmode.offset-el-safe=0` on op-node fixes it, EL sync proceeds normally with no errors.

We were also running op-reth with `--minimal`, which keeps only ~10,064 blocks of history. The default --syncmode.offset-el-safe=12h translates to ~21,600 blocks behind tip at 2s block time — could it be that the offset-derived head is pointing to a block that has already been pruned by --minimal, causing the L1 info deposit tx to appear missing? Would make sense why `--syncmode.offset-el-safe=0` resolves it.

Assumption / hypothesis:
The 12h default seems designed to protect sequencers from marking blocks as safe before L1 confirms them within the sequencing window.
For standard RPC/replica nodes that don't produce blocks, this protection has no meaningful effect, but it does silently break EL sync when paired with any pruned node profile (--minimal, --full) where the offset points beyond the retained history window.

**Suggestion**:
Would it make sense to either document this incompatibility explicitly, or only apply the 12h default when running as a sequencer?

topIssues.title: kona-sp1: dedup derivation prologue against the native fault-proof path
topIssues.author: digorithm
topIssues.body:
Follow-up to #18494. That issue deduped the derivation *loop* (`advance_to_target`); this one covers the derivation *prologue* that precedes it, which is still duplicated across the native fault-proof and kona-sp1 paths.

## Problem

The prologue that sets up derivation is near-identical in (at least) two places, and consensus-critical:

- kona-sp1: [`sp1/crates/client/src/witness/executor.rs:33` (`get_inputs_for_pipeline`)](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/sp1/crates/client/src/witness/executor.rs#L33)
- native single-chain: [`bin/client/src/single.rs:43` (`run`, prologue portion)](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/bin/client/src/single.rs#L43)

Both perform the same sequence:

1. `BootInfo::load`
2. `fetch_safe_head_hash` (see #21657)
3. build `OracleL1ChainProvider` / `OracleL2ChainProvider`
4. `header_by_hash` + `Sealed::new_unchecked` for the safe head
5. reject `claimed_l2_block_number < safe_head.number`
6. trace-extension short-circuit on `claimed_l2_block_number == safe_head.number` (identical `"Trace extension detected. State transition is already agreed upon."` log + the agreed==claimed output-root check)
7. `new_oracle_pipeline_cursor` + `set_cursor`

The cursor-construction tail (steps 6-7) also recurs in the interop path ([`bin/client/src/interop/transition.rs:117`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/bin/client/src/interop/transition.rs#L117)) and the host ([`bin/host/src/interop/handler.rs:578`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89e14a66eff1e6663233b76f5ad75346b270dd53/rust/kona/bin/host/src/interop/handler.rs#L578)).

Duplicating the block-number validation and the trace-extension short-circuit across paths is the same drift risk #18494 addressed for the loop: a fix or hardening applied to one path can silently miss the other.

## Proposed change

Extract a shared prologue helper into `kona-proof` that, given an oracle + boot info, performs steps 1-7 and returns either:

- a "trace extension / zero-step" signal (claim already agreed, no derivation needed), or
- the constructed `(cursor, l1_provider, l2_provider)` ready for pipeline construction.

Then:

- `get_inputs_for_pipeline` (kona-sp1) becomes a thin adapter over it.
- `single.rs::run` calls it, mapping the signal to its `FaultProofProgramError` / `anyhow` error shapes as needed.

## Design considerations

- The two callers differ in shape today: kona-sp1 returns `(BootInfo, Option<(cursor, l1, l2)>)` and builds the pipeline separately; `single.rs` builds inline and uses `FaultProofProgramError` (vs kona-sp1's `anyhow`). The shared helper should return a neutral result the caller maps to its own error type.
- Keep the existing kona-sp1 tests (`get_inputs_for_pipeline_short_circuits_zero_step_claim`, `get_inputs_for_pipeline_rejects_zero_step_root_mismatch`) green; add native-path coverage for the shared helper.
- Interop prologue is a variant (different `BootInfo`/`PreState`); folding it in is a stretch goal, not required for the first pass.

## Acceptance

- One shared prologue helper in a library crate; `get_inputs_for_pipeline` and `single.rs::run` both delegate to it with no duplicated validation/short-circuit logic.
- Existing tests preserved; native + kona-sp1 range guest build and pass.
- Depends on / pairs well with #21657 (shared `fetch_safe_head_hash`).

## Scope

Larger than #21657 and touches consensus-critical validation shared by the native fault-proof program: needs review, not a drive-by.

topPRs.title: op-script-engine: Rust forge-script executor + Go client and parity gates
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Rust `op-script-engine` crate + Go client and byte-parity gates — the base of the op-geth-decoupling script-engine stack (epic #20257 §16). **Additive: no production code selects this engine yet.**

Stack (each stacked on the previous):
1. **this PR** — engine crate, `rustengine` client, parity gates
2. non-forked op-deployer routing + engine default (follows)
3. fork-mode routing + boundary deletion (follows)

### Contents
- **`rust/op-script-engine`** — revm-based re-implementation of the `op-chain-ops/script` EVM host: a cheatcode + console `Inspector`, prank/broadcast capture, forge-artifact loader, state dump, the OPCM `RunScript*` input/output-precompile mechanism, and an RPC-backed fork mode. Served over a UDS JSON-RPC transport (reth-ipc + jsonrpsee).
- **`op-chain-ops/script/rustengine`** — Go client plus A/B parity tests that drive both the Go host and this engine and assert **byte-identical** output: state-dump + broadcast (incl. `gasUsed`), OPCM `RunScriptSingle`/`Void`, and forked `SetDisputeGameImpl` over a hermetic recorded-RPC fixture.
- **Additive helpers** the parity path needs: `script.Precompile` snapshot reflection, `script.Host.ExportDiff`, and a `forking.AccountDiff.Copy` nil-deref fix. `go-tests` provisions the workspace-built binary so the gates run in CI.

### Gates (local)
- `cargo test -p op-script-engine` — 16/16
- `cargo clippy -p op-script-engine --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean; nightly `fmt` clean
- `go test ./op-chain-ops/script/rustengine/` — parity / OPCM / forked / isolated-fork all pass
- base goldens (`TestScriptStateDump|TestScriptBroadcast`) and `./op-chain-ops/script/forking/` unchanged-green

Part of #21743

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

### Review batch applied
Crate hardening (all byte-parity re-validated): contained worker-thread panics (`catch_unwind`); standard precompiles `0x01..=0x0a` no longer framed/broadcast-captured (matches the Go host, which frames only bytecode-bearing targets); `tx.chain_id: None` on raw calls (matches geth's `EVM.Call`, fixes a stale-id case after `vm.chainId`); host setters record into the fork diff when forked; documented that `isolate_broadcast`'s `transaction_id` bump also re-baselines SSTORE originals (revm's cold-slot reset == geth `Finalise(true)`).

Go client hardening: stderr drain uses `bufio.Reader` (no 64KiB line-cap hang); Linux `Pdeathsig=SIGKILL` so a hard-killed test can't leak engines. Test rigor: `TestMain`→`ProvisionTestBinary` + a `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE` guard so the byte-parity gate can't silently skip; a targeted `AccountDiff.Copy` nil-deref regression test; non-vacuity guards on the parity subtests.

**Two flagged potential divergences investigated — both non-divergences:** the implemented cheatcode set is complete for the OPCM-routed scripts (env*/toString/parseJson/file-IO are used only by the legacy forge scripts, never routed; verified by the passing full-suite A/B gates), and the isolated-broadcast SSTORE-original re-baseline is handled by revm (source-confirmed).

**One real divergence found — access control:** enforcing Go's cheatcode access control naively breaks byte parity, because the routed deploy scripts deploy helper contracts that call cheatcodes and rely on Go's transitive auto-grant-on-deploy. Left **unenforced** (the current byte-parity-correct behavior, documented in `cheatcodes.rs`); correct enforcement needs the auto-grant replicated and is a dedicated follow-up.

topPRs.title: chore: bump reth to include #26398 fix (validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Josh Klopfenstein** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0A3E04GDMX/p1784054235311919?thread_ts=1784054235.311919&cid=C0A3E04GDMX)_

Refs #21524

## Before

The Rust workspaces pinned `paradigmxyz/reth` to the **`v2.3.0`** release tag. reth `v2.4.0` shipped an incidental change to `validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state` that broke the OP Stack, so we could not simply move to the `v2.4.0` tag.

## After

The reth pin is moved to **`rev = "f2eecc65482af4085e43eedb27a32024bf177a0d"`** — the merge commit of paradigmxyz/reth#26398 (Sebastian Stammler's fix), which landed on `main` *after* the `v2.4.0` tag. This restores the `validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state` signature the OP Stack needs while picking up the rest of the 2.4.0 line. Because the fix is post-tag, we pin the commit (`rev`) rather than a tag, per `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md`.

Note this is a **two-release catch-up** (`v2.3.0` → post-`v2.4.0`), not a one-commit nudge — see "Remaining work" below.

## How

- Bump the reth git ref from `tag = "v2.3.0"` to `rev = "f2eecc65…"` across all **four** manifests the guide enumerates: `rust/Cargo.toml`, `rust/op-rbuilder/Cargo.toml`, `rust/rollup-boost/crates/rollup-boost/Cargo.toml`, `rust/rollup-boost/crates/flashblocks-rpc/Cargo.toml` (122 pin lines total).
- Sync the shared crates.io dependency versions to reth's pins at the new rev (read from reth's `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` at `f2eecc65…`):
  - `revm` family `40.x` → **`41.0.0`** (upstream unified all `revm-*` subcrates to `41.0.0`), `revm-inspectors` `0.40.1` → `0.41.0`; in `op-rbuilder`, `revm-context`/`revm-context-interface`/`revm-inspector` → `41.0.0`.
  - published reth-core crates (`reth-codecs`, `reth-codecs-derive`, `reth-primitives-traits`, `reth-rpc-traits`, `reth-zstd-compressors`) `0.4.1` → **`0.5.0`**.
  - alloy core (`alloy-consensus` … `alloy-transport*`) `2.0.x` → **`2.1.1`**, `alloy-evm` `0.36.0` → `0.37.0`, `alloy-eip7928` `0.4.0` → `0.4.5`, `alloy-rlp` `0.3.13` → `0.3.16`, `alloy-primitives`/`alloy-sol-types` bumped to `1.6.0` where they lagged.
  - OP-internal path crates (`op-revm`, `op-alloy*`, `alloy-op-evm`, `alloy-op-hardforks`) left untouched, per the guide.
- Update the replicated `SlotPreimages` MDBX-layout rev reference in `rust/op-reth/crates/cli/src/commands/slot_preimages_seed.rs`. I diffed the upstream `slot_preimages.rs` between `9384bc53…` (v2.3.0) and `f2eecc65…`: the byte-layout and insert/read logic are **identical** — only visibility (`pub`) and docs changed — so the replica stays byte-compatible and only the rev comment moved. (The upstream type becoming `pub` is what unblocks removing the replica in #21523.)

## Verification

⚠️ **Not built/resolved in this environment.** `cargo update` / `cargo check` against the new rev cannot run here: outbound git access to `github.com/paradigmxyz/reth` is blocked by egress policy (HTTP 403 through the agent proxy). Consequently:

- **Lockfiles are NOT regenerated** — the three `Cargo.lock` files still record the `v2.3.0` git source. They must be refreshed in an environment with reth access (`cargo update reth-chainspec` in `.`, `op-rbuilder/`, and `rollup-boost/`).
- The **compile-and-adapt loop was not run.** A two-release reth jump routinely requires op-side source adaptations (trait-method params, struct destructuring, re-export/rename churn — see `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md`). None of that is in this PR yet.

## Remaining work (before un-drafting)

1. Regenerate all three lockfiles against the new rev.
2. Run the compile-and-adapt loop to green across all three workspaces (`cargo check --workspace --tests`), then `cargo build -p op-reth`, `just fmt-fix`, `just lint`, `just test`.
3. Consider folding in #21523 (drop the replicated `SlotPreimages` now that upstream is `pub`).
4. Run the reth-update AI review (`docs/ai/reth-update-review.md`).

Draft until the above lands and CI is green.

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: delete the Go script engine
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
**CLI break:** the `--script-engine` / `DEPLOYER_SCRIPT_ENGINE` flag is gone (on `op-deployer apply`, `bootstrap`, `inspect l2-semvers`, `manage`, `upgrade`, and `op-fetcher`). It never shipped in a released `op-deployer`; with one engine there is nothing to select.

**Cross-repo compile break:** deleting `scriptbackend.FromHost` and the `FetchChainInfo(*script.Host, …)` signature (now only `FetchChainInfoWithBackend(scriptbackend.Backend, …)`) breaks the external superchain-registry `ops` module the next time it bumps its `optimism` pin past this commit. It is deliberate — the Go host is gone — but needs a coordinated downstream update (switch the caller to `FetchChainInfoWithBackend`).

Deletes the Go script engine so the Rust `op-script-engine` is the only implementation. This lets `op-chain-ops/script` drop every geth `core/vm | state | trie | triedb | tracers | ethdb` import — the blocker for depending on upstream go-ethereum (§16 of #20257).

Three commits:
1. **goldenize** — record the live Go host's outputs (allocs JSON, broadcast lists, fork diffs) from the base tip as committed fixtures and convert every A/B parity gate into a Rust-vs-fixture golden regression test. The safety net survives the host's deletion. CI arms it: the go-test jobs set `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE=1` so a missing engine binary fails the golden gates loudly instead of skipping the sole post-deletion proof of the Go host's behavior.
2. **delete** — remove the in-process geth-EVM host machinery in `op-chain-ops/script` (host EVM, cheatcode precompile dispatch, prank machinery), `op-chain-ops/script/forking` (~2088 LOC RPC ForkDB), the Go arms behind the flag, and Go-only host tests. Tests that constructed Go forked hosts are migrated to the Rust engine or deleted with written rationale.
3. **flag removal** — delete the `op-deployer/pkg/env` script-engine package and the flag/param plumbing (`scriptbackend.NewForkedL1`, `interopgen.Deploy`, the interopgen host factory).

Kept (the Rust path depends on them): `script.Context`, Broadcast types + JSON, the foundry artifacts packages, the Precompile reflection machinery, ABI helpers, `DeployScript` wrappers, the `rustengine` package.

Local sweep green: `go test ./op-chain-ops/...`, the goldens (L2Genesis 5 modes, pipeline L1/L2, 9 forks, semvers, interopgen, rustengine, scriptbackend) run under `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE=1` with the pre-built binary, `op-e2e/config`, `op-e2e/interop TestInteropDevRecipe`, `cargo test -p op-script-engine`. Remaining `./op-deployer/...` failures are pre-existing environmental gates (network `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL`, forge recompile, a missing local artifact) that also fail on the base and do not reach any changed code.

Part of #21743
